deliverable.title: import ppo_lite crashes on a clean install — the package can't even be loaded
deliverable.detail: ppo_lite/__init__.py eagerly does `from .gae import compute_gae`, and gae.py does a top-level `import numpy` (and torch). numpy/torch are declared in NO manifest. In a clean environment `import ppo_lite` raises ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'numpy'. The probe's `pytest -q` exits rc=2 — a COLLECTION error, not a test failure: tests/test_losses.py can't import the package at all. The org's reviewed DoD passed only because the engineer worktrees happened to have numpy/torch installed; the landed deliverable is import-broken.

deliverable.title: The train(env) loop is REINFORCE, not PPO
deliverable.detail: train() in train.py computes loss = -(logp * reward) — a one-step vanilla policy gradient on the immediate reward. It never calls ppo_losses, never uses the clipped surrogate objective, never uses GAE advantages, and never touches the RolloutBuffer. The brief's single headline deliverable — a PPO train loop — does not implement PPO. The three real PPO pieces sit in the repo unused.

deliverable.title: GAE is implemented twice, in two incompatible numeric substrates
deliverable.detail: gae.py::compute_gae implements GAE in torch (returns torch.FloatTensor). buffer.py::RolloutBuffer.compute_returns_and_advantages re-implements the identical GAE recursion in numpy (plus advantage normalization). Two independent copies of the same algorithm; buffer.py never calls compute_gae. Both recursions are individually correct — which makes the duplication purely an integration failure, not a math error.

deliverable.title: The three brief-required surfaces are not exported
deliverable.detail: __init__ exports only PPOConfig, compute_gae, seed_everything. The clipped surrogate (ppo_losses), the rollout buffer (RolloutBuffer), and the train loop (train) — the three things the brief explicitly required — are NOT in __all__ and not imported into the package namespace. `from ppo_lite import ppo_losses / RolloutBuffer / train` all fail; a user must reach into private submodules.

deliverable.title: PPOConfig (all the PPO hyperparameters) is exported but unused; train uses a different config
deliverable.detail: config.py defines PPOConfig with gamma, gae_lambda, clip_coef, vf_coef, ent_coef, lr, update_epochs, minibatch_size… But train() takes a separate TrainConfig(seed, total_steps, lr) and ignores PPOConfig entirely. So every PPO knob is dead. There's also a name mismatch: PPOConfig.clip_coef vs ppo_losses(clip_range=…) — they wouldn't line up even if someone tried to wire them.

deliverable.title: Four components, three numeric substrates — they don't compose
deliverable.detail: gae.py and train.py are torch; losses.py is pure-Python floats (its docstring: “dependency-free … minimal environments”); buffer.py is numpy. compute_gae emits torch tensors while ppo_losses consumes float lists — you cannot feed one into the other without manual conversion. Each engineer picked a different substrate and nothing reconciled them.

deliverable.title: No packaging and undeclared heavy dependencies
deliverable.detail: No pyproject.toml / setup.py / setup.cfg of any kind. The package imports torch (gae.py, train.py) and numpy (gae.py, buffer.py) but declares neither. It is neither installable nor reproducible.

deliverable.title: README stub + stray + leaked files
deliverable.detail: README.md is the 15-byte seed stub “# company repo”. Root test_smoke.py (`assert True`) sits outside tests/. ~24 harness-internal files leaked (docs/evals/*.json, docs/exec-plans/*).

framework.title: Three deliverable tasks handed to the analyst → all three rejected
framework.detail: The analyst (a non-coding role) was assigned three implementation tasks and rejected all three. The manager repeated the same mis-route three times instead of escalating to an engineer.

framework.title: No cross-child file ownership — the cause of the semantic split-brain
framework.detail: The two GAE implementations, the two configs, and the orphaned losses/buffer are the direct symptom: each engineer authored a slice (gae/losses/buffer/train) on its own branch, and integrate merged them without anyone owning the package's public surface or reconciling the substrates. Note the duplication is SEMANTIC (two GAEs in differently-named files) — a filename-collision check can't see it; only reading the code does.

framework.title: The DoD passed in a richer env than the deliverable ships in
framework.detail: The reviewed-build DoD went green in engineer worktrees where numpy/torch were present, but the landed package is import-broken in a clean environment and the train loop is off-brief (REINFORCE). The gate verified “tests pass in my worktree,” not “the deliverable installs, imports, and does PPO” — so a non-installable, non-PPO package passed.
